name: antenatal care overview
title: Antenatal care from first suspicion to term: what to assess, test and act on at each stage (confirm and date, first visit, second trimester, third trimester), then how the first-visit group and screen splits into Rh negative without an antibody (Rh immunoglobulin) and an antibody found (titre, middle cerebral artery Doppler, timing of delivery); panels on checking a medication or exposure and on who cares for her

nodes.title: Antenatal care: what do I assess, test and act on at THIS visit?
lines: after 20 weeks, ANY headache or sudden severe edema: exclude preeclampsia → HYPERTENSION chart
lifestyle, food, nausea and safe medicines: see the EARLY PREGNANCY COUNSELLING chart

nodes.title: Visit by visit, in order
lines: each stage adds to the last

nodes.title: The first-visit GROUP AND SCREEN decides
lines: is she Rh negative, and is there an ANTIBODY?

nodes.title: 1 · Suspect, confirm, date
lines: before the first visit

nodes.title: 2 · First visit
lines: first trimester, to 14 weeks

nodes.title: 3 · Second trimester
lines: 14–28 weeks

nodes.title: 4 · Third trimester → term
lines: 28 weeks on

nodes.title: Rh NEGATIVE, no antibody
lines: Rh immunoglobulin (RhIG) PREVENTS one

nodes.title: ANTIBODY found
lines: it can cross the placenta: fetal anemia

nodes.title: Missed period
lines: the first sign if cycles are regular
irregular cycles or on the pill: spotting or lighter menses instead
symptoms alone never confirm it

nodes.title: GTPAL
lines: gravida (incl. this one) · term ≥ 37 wk · preterm 20–37 wk
abortions < 20 wk · living children

nodes.title: Also ask
lines: every medication + exposure → MEDICATION panel
cramps ± spotting → FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart

nodes.title: Fundus
lines: at the UMBILICUS by 20 weeks
then symphysis-fundus height (cm) ≈ weeks

nodes.title: Spotting: normal or assess?
lines: normal: liner only, on wiping, brownish; after walking, exercise, sex
ASSESS: frank red, fills a pad, pain, contractions, trauma

nodes.title: Contractions: labour or not?
lines: LABOUR: rhythmic, regular, 20–60 s, minutes apart, stronger
Braxton Hicks: painless, sporadic, nonrhythmic

nodes.title: Abdominal pain: rule out
lines: placental abruption · preeclampsia + HELLP (hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets) · acute fatty liver
after ANY trauma: seen in person

nodes.title: Fetal cells reach her blood
lines: RhIG clears them before she makes an antibody
useless once an antibody exists

nodes.title: Why, and will the fetus carry it?
lines: previous pregnancy · transfusion · drug use
screen the partner (zygosity)

nodes.title: 1 · Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), urine or serum
lines: serum > 25 = pregnant · most useful: irregular cycles, recurrent miscarriage, previous ectopic
2 · where is it? → FIRST-TRIMESTER BLEEDING chart

nodes.title: 1 · For ALL
lines: complete blood count · group and screen · rubella immunity
hepatitis B · HIV · syphilis · gonorrhea + chlamydia · urine culture
11–14 wk: genetic screen → PRENATAL GENETIC SCREENING chart

nodes.title: 2 · Only if selected
lines: thyroid-stimulating hormone: known thyroid disease
hemoglobinopathy: Mediterranean, Southeast Asian, African, or low mean cell volume

nodes.title: Anatomy scan, 18–22 weeks
lines: → ULTRASOUND THROUGH PREGNANCY chart
low-lying placenta or previa: ANY spotting is investigated

nodes.title: Recheck hemoglobin + ferritin
lines: low: anemia work-up + iron on the PHYSIOLOGIC CHANGES chart

nodes.title: 1 · Titre < 1/8
lines: repeat MONTHLY

nodes.title: 1 · Titre ≥ 1/8
lines: risk of SEVERE anemia

nodes.title: 2 · Middle cerebral artery Doppler
lines: peak systolic velocity tracks fetal hemoglobin
worse: polyhydramnios, hydrops

nodes.title: Set the due date EARLY
lines: Naegele: last normal menstrual period + 7 days − 3 months + 1 year
dating scan → ULTRASOUND THROUGH PREGNANCY chart

nodes.title: Prenatal multivitamin DAILY
lines: folic acid (600 mcg) + iron (27 mg): most often needed
+350–450 kcal/day: healthy eating over weight gain

nodes.title: Vaccinate EVERY pregnancy
lines: pertussis (Tdap) at 27–32 wk: her antibodies protect the baby
influenza: any week, in flu season

nodes.title: NO live vaccines → post-partum
lines: measles-mumps-rubella · varicella · bacille Calmette-Guérin

nodes.title: Give RhIG
lines: 1 · ROUTINELY at 28–30 weeks
2 · post-partum if the baby is Rh POSITIVE

nodes.title: Also after bleeding, a procedure or trauma
lines: from 8–10 weeks

nodes.title: 1 · Early + severe anemia
lines: intrauterine transfusion of antigen-negative blood, serially

nodes.title: 2 · Severe anemia after 34–35 wk
lines: deliver

panels.title: Medication or exposure at any visit: what to check
items: WHEN: weeks 1–2 insensitive · weeks 3–8 (organogenesis) → MAJOR anomalies · later → function + minor anomalies
WHAT: radiation, hyperthermia · TORCH infections · maternal diabetes · drugs, herbals, recreational drugs, toxins
US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) category: A human studies safe · D human risk, benefit may win · X risk outweighs any benefit
Planning pregnancy: optimize the disease · fewest drugs, lowest dose · switch if possible · folic acid 1 mg on antiepileptics · ask FRAME (Fetal Risk After Maternal Exposure)

panels.title: Who looks after her
items: LOW risk: family physician (cares for the baby too, for years) or midwife (home, birth centre or hospital; mother + baby to 6 weeks)
CONSULT obstetrics: diabetes, essential hypertension, prior preeclampsia, high body mass index, lupus · abnormal fetal surveillance · planned cesarean
labour: dystocia, operative or cesarean birth, preeclampsia · post-partum: major hemorrhage, 3rd/4th-degree tear
